title: Scams aimed at service members and veterans
summary: New York's attorney general published a guide to scams that target the military community, including people who charge veterans to "help" with VA claims, offers of quick cash in exchange for pension payments, overpriced financing sold per pay period, and fake charities.
what_to_do: Don't pay anyone to help file your first VA claim, and check any benefits message by logging in to your official account directly.

sources.name: New York Attorney General: Scams targeting the military

title: Callers pressuring employees to use Bitcoin ATMs
summary: Police in Ocean City, Md., say scammers are calling hotels, complimenting staff and offering a "bonus" for settling a supposed balance with cash from the register or safe through a Bitcoin ATM.
what_to_do: Tell staff that the business owner will never ask them to pay a balance with cash from the register or safe through a Bitcoin ATM. Report any such call to police.

sources.name: CoastTV, reporting the Ocean City Police Department warning

title: Fake FBI agents calling from real FBI numbers
summary: FBI Honolulu warned that scammers are posing as FBI, DEA and Secret Service agents and faking the phone numbers of real FBI offices, so calling back the number can still reach the scammer. Victims are threatened with arrest and told to pay. In one case, the scammer used a video call with a background made to look like a federal office.
what_to_do: Hang up, look up the agency's number yourself, and never pay anyone who says they're a government officer, since real agencies don't demand payment by phone, prepaid card, cryptocurrency or courier.

sources.name: Maui Now, reporting the FBI Honolulu warning (Nov 2, 2026)
FBI IC3 Public Service Announcement I-091726-PSA

title: Fake FTC calls threaten to shut off your phone
summary: The FTC warned that callers posing as FTC officials claim a phone number in your name was used for scams in another country and threaten to disconnect your phone. They transfer you to a fake police officer, tell you to keep the call secret, then claim you're under arrest and demand a "security deposit."
what_to_do: Hang up. Real FTC employees never ask for money, threaten to cut off your phone or tell you to keep a call secret. Report the call to the FTC.

sources.name: FTC: The FTC is not calling to deactivate your phone number

title: Fake campaign "investments" and scam PACs
summary: The FBI warned that scammers are using the midterm elections to run fake campaign investment pools, pose as political action committees, sell merchandise that never ships, and send fake voter registration messages. Some use AI-generated voices of candidates.
what_to_do: Donations are never investments. Check a committee on the Federal Election Commission's website before giving, and confirm your registration on the official federal voter registration site.

sources.name: FBI IC3 Public Service Announcement I-101526-3-PSA
